d: 🥗 Food Quality Manager / Food Safety Manager
Job Level: Management / Food Quality & Safety Operations

We are seeking a knowledgeable, detail-oriented, and results-driven Food Quality Manager / Food Safety Manager to oversee food quality standards, safety procedures, and compliance across daily operations. The ideal candidate will ensure that food products meet regulatory requirements, maintain high hygiene standards, and follow effective quality control processes while promoting continuous improvement throughout the organization.
Develop, implement, and monitor food quality and food safety management systems.
Ensure food products comply with applicable food safety regulations and industry standards.
Oversee food inspections, quality testing, and hygiene monitoring procedures.
Implement and maintain food safety programs, including HACCP and relevant ISO standards.
Conduct regular facility inspections, internal audits, and food safety assessments.
Monitor food handling, storage, preparation, packaging, and distribution processes.
Investigate food safety incidents, customer complaints, and quality-related issues.
Identify risks and implement corrective and preventive actions.
Supervise and train staff on food safety, sanitation, and quality procedures.
Maintain accurate quality records, inspection reports, and compliance documentation.
Coordinate with suppliers and operational teams to ensure ingredient and product quality.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen food quality and safety performance.
Relevant qualifications in Food Science, Food Technology, Food Safety, Quality Management, or a related discipline.
Strong knowledge of food safety regulations, hygiene practices, and quality control procedures.
Understanding of HACCP, ISO 22000, and other relevant food safety standards.
Ability to conduct inspections, audits, risk assessments, and quality evaluations.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Good leadership and team management abilities.
High attention to detail and commitment to food safety and quality standards.
Opportunities to lead food quality and safety improvement initiatives.
Exposure to food safety management systems and regulatory compliance.
Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

The Inventory Analyst is responsible for maintaining accurate inventory and item master data, preparing operational and management reports, developing dashboards, and supporting inventory planning and analysis across Kuwait and GCC operations.
r: Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly inventory reports covering stock position, aging, near-expiry and expiry, wastage, variances, turnover, stock coverage, and slow/non-moving items.
Analyze inventory trends and highlight shortages, excess stock, expiry exposure, abnormal consumption, stock imbalances, and material variances.

Support the setting and periodic review of Min/Max levels, reorder parameters, safety stock, forecasting inputs, and inventory-planning assumptions in coordination with Supply Chain, Procurement, Warehouse, and Operations.
Provide accurate analysis for inventory actions, including replenishment, redistribution, liquidation, write-off review, cycle counting, and corrective measures.

Create, maintain, and update item/SKU codes and master data, including item descriptions, UOM, pack size, category, brand, specifications, shelf life, storage requirements, and relevant planning attributes.
Maintain inventory master data across ERP, SUPY, and approved reporting systems, ensuring controlled changes and alignment with Finance, Procurement, Warehouse, and Operations.
Perform data-quality checks and coordinate resolution of duplicate items, incorrect descriptions, inconsistent UOMs, pack-size errors, inactive items, mapping issues, and system discrepancies.
Maintain clear documentation of data changes, approvals, effective dates, ownership, and dependencies.

Coordinate the GCC-wide Item Unification Project to establish a common item structure, standardized descriptions, UOMs, pack sizes, categories, brands, specifications, and item-status rules across markets.
Create and maintain the project mapping between existing country items and unified GCC items, identifying duplicates, near-duplicates, obsolete items, conversion factors, and unresolved exceptions.
Work with regional Supply Chain, Procurement, Warehouse, Finance, IT, Operations, and other data owners to validate proposed unified items and secure timely approvals.
Maintain the project tracker, issue log, decision register, data dictionary, implementation milestones, and market sign-offs; escalate delays, conflicting requirements, and material data risks.
Support controlled implementation, user communication, testing, reconciliation, and post-implementation validation to ensure reporting and transaction integrity are preserved.
Develop and maintain Excel dashboards and management reports for inventory, aging, expiry, wastage, variances, turnover, stock coverage, and master-data quality.
Ensure reports are accurate, timely, clearly defined, and based on approved data sources and calculation logic.
Identify opportunities for reporting automation, improved data flow, reduced manual effort, and better visibility of inventory risks and actions.
Provide ad hoc analysis and management insights when required, with clear assumptions, conclusions, and recommended actions.
